106. At this point, it is essential to distinguish between retrospective and retroactive laws.

65 For example, if a law prohibits houses from having more than two floors and requires existing houses exceeding this limit to be demolished, it is retrospective.
If the law only affects houses under construction when it comes into force, it is retroactive.

As we look at it, Article 30(1) is a sort of guarantee or assurance to the linguistic and religious minority institutions of their right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.

No law can be framed that will discriminate against such minorities with regard to the establishment and administration of educational institutions vis-a-vis other educational institutions.

In other words, the essence of Article 30(1) is to ensure equal treatment between the majority and the minority institutions.
No one type or category of institution should be disfavoured or, for that matter, receive more favourable treatment than another.
Laws of the land, including rules and regulations, must apply equally to the majority institutions as well as to the minority institutions.
The minority institutions must be allowed to do what the non-minority institutions are permitted to do.
